items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: I used to tell people that I taught Charlie Parker how to play and they’d look at me like I was crazy or something, you know.

ctx.x: Yeah. On one of your albums, you have a tune called “The Fiddler” where you mix jazz inflections with country influences. Tell us about that.

Well “The Fiddler” is just actually a type of blues and with different changes and things you add to it, you know. Like [sings] every three or four notes, or every measure you play a different change. But it still starts from a blues idea. And as I tell people, Charlie Parker came up, you know, in Kansas City and I used to tell people that I taught Charlie Parker how to play and they’d look at me like I was crazy or something, you know. But Charlie, every time you’d see him he’d have his horn in a sack and his…
So you helped him with his chord vocabulary?
